title: Adjectives & Adverbs: Degrees
subtitle: clārus, clāra, clārum (clear): positive, comparative and superlative
intro:
Adjectives and adverbs have three degrees: positive (clear), comparative (clearer) and superlative (clearest). All three are built on the stem clār-.
  • Positive: clārus, clāra, clārum, declined like the 1st and 2nd declensions (equus, puella, forum).
  • Comparative: stem + -ior (masculine and feminine) / -ius (neuter), then 3rd-declension endings on the stem clāriōr-: clāriōris, clāriōrī, clāriōrem, clāriōre; plural clāriōrēs, clāriōrum, clāriōribus. Neuter plural nominative and accusative: clāriōra.
  • Superlative: stem + -issimus, -issima, -issimum, declined like clārus.

Adverbs:

  • From 1st/2nd-declension adjectives: stem + -ē: clārē (clearly).
  • From 3rd-declension adjectives: stem + -iter: fortiter (bravely), ācriter, celeriter, fēlīciter.
  • Comparative adverb = the neuter comparative adjective: clārius, fortius. Superlative: -issimē (clārissimē), or -errimē for adjectives in -er (ācerrimē, celerrimē).
  • Irregular: bene, melius, optimē · male, peius, pessimē · multum, plūs, plūrimum · magnopere, magis, maximē · parum, minus, minimē · facile, facilius, facillimē · saepe, saepius, saepissimē · diū, diūtius, diūtissimē.

Watch out: clārius is both the neuter comparative adjective and the comparative adverb. Context decides. The comparative can also mean “rather clear” or “too clear”, and the superlative “very clear”.
